title: Cohomology modules of a coefficient complex
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ and the stagewise $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)=\operatorname{2-colim}_{E'\in\mathcal E_\ell}D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E')$ be the finite coefficient categories over a point [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For a ring $R$, an object $C$ of the derived category $D(R)$ of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and an integer $i$, write $\mathrm H^i(C)=\ker(d^i)/\operatorname{im}(d^{i-1})$ for the $i$-th cohomology module of any complex representing $C$; it is an $R$-module, well defined up to canonical isomorphism since quasi-isomorphisms induce isomorphisms on cohomology, and $C\mapsto\mathrm H^i(C)$ is a functor $D(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$. For $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$, $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ and $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, the cohomology modules $\mathrm H^i(C)$ are this functor applied to $C$: a finite $A_{E,n}$-module, a finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-module, and a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space respectively. For an object of $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ represented at the stage $E'\in\mathcal E_\ell$ by $C'\in D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E')$, define

$$
 \mathrm H^i(C)=\mathrm H^i(C')\otimes_{E'}\Qlb,
$$

a finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector space; a change of stage $E'\subset L$ replaces $C'$ by $C'\otimes_{E'}L$, and the canonical isomorphism $\mathrm H^i(C'\otimes_{E'}L)\otimes_L\Qlb\cong\mathrm H^i(C')\otimes_{E'}\Qlb$ (cohomology commutes with the exact functor $-\otimes_{E'}L$) identifies the two definitions, so $\mathrm H^i(C)$ is well defined up to canonical isomorphism, and a morphism of $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$, represented over a common stage, induces a $\Qlb$-linear map on $\mathrm H^i$.
